paper_metadata.title: Research on the influence of ultra-low temperature extreme environments on the surface quality and fatigue life of FeCoCrNiAl0.6 high entropy alloy

It is believed that during low-temperature cutting, the environmental temperature is low, which can be considered as cryogenic treatment of the material. In the cutting process, the low-temperature environment effectively reduces the temperature in the cutting zone, making the material locally brittle, decreasing its plasticity and toughness, thereby facilitating chip breaking and parting, enhancing chip breaking, and simultaneously reducing tool wear, thereby improving the damage to the already machined surface

The local low-temperature environment can enhance the material’s brittleness, weaken the plastic deformation capacity of the processed surface, thereby reducing the surface roughness. The smoother the machining surface, the fewer indentations, the more evenly distributed the stress, thus less likely to crack or similar phenomena, prolonging the usage time, enhancing fatigue resistance, and thereby improving fatigue strength.
